title: Indiana's 3rd Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: Indiana's 3rd Congressional District covers all or parts of 12 counties in northeast Indiana, including the city of Fort Wayne. Incumbent Republican Rep. Marlin Stutzman faces Democratic challenger Kelly Thompson in the November 3, 2026 general election. Stutzman won the Republican primary on May 5, 2026, defeating challenger Jon Kenworthy with 68.2% of the vote, while Thompson ran unopposed for the Democratic nomination. The Cook Political Report rates this race as "Solidly Republican," giving Stutzman a strong advantage in the heavily conservative district. Key issues in the race include inflation, healthcare costs, housing affordability, and federal spending.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of mid-June 2026. The Cook Political Report rates Indiana's 3rd District as 'Solidly Republican,' consistent with the district's voting history.

candidates.name: Marlin Stutzman
candidates.summary: Marlin Stutzman is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Indiana's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in a 2010 special election and serving again since 2025 after a prior tenure from 2010 to 2017. A fourth-generation farmer and business owner from Howe, Indiana, he co-owns Stutzman Farms and a trucking company, and previously served in the Indiana House of Representatives (2003–2009) and Indiana Senate (2009–2010). In Congress, he serves on the House Financial Services and Budget Committees and is a member of the Freedom Caucus, focusing on fiscal conservatism, agricultural policy, and reducing federal regulations.

candidates.name: Kelly Thompson
candidates.summary: Kelly Thompson is the Democratic nominee for U.S. House in Indiana's 3rd Congressional District. A business owner and non-profit founder from Columbia City, Indiana, she describes herself as a 'Hoosier wife, mother, business owner and non-profit founder' fighting for working families. Thompson ran unopposed in the Democratic primary on May 5, 2026. Her campaign priorities include protecting farmland, lowering healthcare costs, making affordable housing more available, legalizing cannabis, and reforming campaign finance.

forecast.rationale: No public polls exist for this race, keeping confidence at medium and requiring reliance on structural indicators. Those indicators overwhelmingly favor Republicans: incumbent Marlin Stutzman represents a heavily conservative district, won his primary decisively (68.2%), and the Cook Political Report rates the seat Solidly Republican. Democratic challenger Kelly Thompson, a first-time candidate who ran unopposed in the primary, faces steep structural headwinds in a district where the GOP has a deep voter registration and partisan advantage. Without any polling evidence of a competitive shift, a Stutzman victory remains highly probable.
